page: Amazon Web Services m8in.8xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 128.0 GB, yielding a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for general computing demands.

The instance does not include local NVMe or SSD storage and relies entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Networking capabilities are highlighted by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating high-throughput data transfer between infrastructure components. Hardware acceleration is not present, as the configuration provides zero GPUs and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the m8in.8xlarge pairs dense x86 compute with high baseline networking without the overhead costs associated with onboard storage arrays. The primary operational tradeoff is complete dependency on external storage volumes for disk operations, offset by the broad network pipe. Appropriate workloads include network-intensive backend services, container clusters, intermediate database systems, and enterprise application deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8in.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor offering 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated physical cores with multithreading support. The system provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage, instead utilizing network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps, and no GPU accelerators are included. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware tier delivers dense compute and high networking capacity without the added expense of idle local storage controllers. With its balanced processor and memory configuration, m8in.8xlarge is well positioned for enterprise application servers, mid-sized relational database hosting, container orchestration worker nodes, and network-intensive backend services.
